# Introduction

CSSpatialNet is a method for estimation of cell-type-specific spatial 
autocorrelations and gene covariances from spot-level spatial data. The method
works by fitting a spatially autoregressive model on each cell type's gene
expression matrix, including a non-spatial multivariate normal error term for 
the gene covariances. The spatial autocorrelations and (non-spatial) gene 
covariances are estimated through maximum likelihood estimation. The resulting 
parameter estimates can be used to better understand gene-gene covariances in a
way that accounts for the spatial autocorrelation of genes in spatial biology. 
The method allows for calculating the standard error of each parameter, which 
can be used to construct confidence intervals or perform hypothesis tests.

## Method overview

1) Set up model
2) Maximum likelihood with ADAM optimiser for parameter estimation
3) Standard errors calculated with Fisher information

## Vignette overview

# Data

## Simulated Data

For this vignette, we generate a small simulated dataset to demonstrate 
CSSpatialNet's capabilities. For this simulation, we will have $n = 100$ points,
$p = 2$ genes, and $K = 2$ cell types. $P_k$, the spatial autocorrelation vector 
for cell type $k$ and $\Sigma_k$, the gene-gene covariance matrix for cell type
$k$, are constructed as follows:

$$P_1 = (0,0.7), P_2 = (0.8,0.4)$$
$$\Sigma_1 = \begin{bmatrix}1.2 & 0.5 \\0.5 & 1\end{bmatrix},
\Sigma_2 = \begin{bmatrix}1.5 & 0 \\0 & 0.8\end{bmatrix}$$

The $n = 100$ points are equally spaced on a $10 \times 10$ grid. The spatial 
weights, as by default, are constructed to be an adjacency matrix where there is
an edge between points that are adjacent or diagonally opposite. The adjacency 
matrix is row normalised, made symmetric, and then the largest eigenvalue is set
to be 0. These are needed for the estimation procedure to hold.

We then randomly generate each cell type's gene expression matrix under the
correct model. 

```{r}
n <- 225
p <- 2
K <- 2
P1 <- diag(c(0, 0.7))
P2 <- diag(c(0.8, 0.4))

Sigma1 <- matrix(c(1.2,0.5,0.5,1), nrow = 2)
Sigma2 <- matrix(c(1.5,0,0,0.8), nrow = 2)

coords_df <- expand.grid(c(1:sqrt(n)), c(1:sqrt(n)))/sqrt(n)

# create spatial weight matrix
weights <- CSSpatialNet:::create_weights(coords = coords_df, lattice_shape = "square")

# Create covariance matrix of vec(X) for cell type 1
Ainv_ct1 <- solve(diag(n*p) - kronecker(P1, weights))
cov_mat_vecX_ct1 <- Ainv_ct1 %*% kronecker(Sigma1, diag(n)) %*% Ainv_ct1

# Create covariance matrix of vec(X) for cell type 2
Ainv_ct2 <- solve(diag(n*p) - kronecker(P2, weights))
cov_mat_vecX_ct2 <- Ainv_ct2 %*% kronecker(Sigma2, diag(n)) %*% Ainv_ct2

# create proportions
props_mat <- rdirichlet(n = n, alpha = rep(5, 2))

# create the per-cell-type and spot-level gene expression matrices
vecX_ct1 <- mvnfast::rmvn(n = 1,
                          mu = rep(0, n*p),
                          sigma = cov_mat_vecX_ct1)
X_ct1 <- matrix(vecX_ct1, nrow = n, ncol = p)
vecX_ct2 <- mvnfast::rmvn(n = 1,
                          mu = rep(0, n*p),
                          sigma = cov_mat_vecX_ct2)
X_ct2 <- matrix(vecX_ct2, nrow = n, ncol = p)
vecX <- vecX_ct1 * rep(props_mat[,1], p) +
  vecX_ct2 * rep(props_mat[,2], p)
X <- matrix(vecX, nrow = n, ncol = p)

# cov(X)
# CSNet::mom_ls(X = X, P = props_mat, weight_th = 0.01)
```

Below is displayed the expression of gene 1 within each cell type and in the 
spot-level dataset. It is important to note that this gene has no spatial
autocorrelation in cell type 1, since $P_1[1] = 0$, which corresponds to no 
clear pattern in the first facet. There is spatial autocorrelation for cell type 
2, since $P_2[1] \neq 0$, corresponding to a visible clumping in the middle
facet. The spot-level expression has a mild level of clumping. CSSpatialNet
attemps to recover the spatial autocorrelation for each gene within each cell
type, while also estimating the gene-gene covariance matrices.

```{r}
X_df <- data.frame(g1 = c(X_ct1[,1],X_ct2[,1],X[,1]),
                        g2 = c(X_ct1[,2],X_ct2[,2],X[,2]),
                        spatial1 = rep(coords_df$Var1, 3),
                        spatial2 = rep(coords_df$Var2, 3),
                        group = vec_rep_each(c("Cell type 1",
                                               "Cell type 2",
                                               "Spot"), n))

ggplot(X_df, aes(x = spatial1, y = spatial2, colour = g1)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c() +
  facet_wrap(vars(group)) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(x = "Spatial 1",
       y = "Spatial 2",
       colour = "Gene 1") +
  ggtitle("Spot-level and within-cell-type expression of gene 1")
```

# CSSpatialNet for spatial autocorrelation and gene-gene covariance estimation

## CSSpatialNet computation

Below we run CSSpatialNet on the simulated data we created before.

```{r}
set.seed(2026)
csspatialnet_out <- CSSpatialNet(X = X,
                                 proportions = props_mat,
                                 W = weights,
                                 print_every = 50)
# csspatialnet_out$SEs

CI_dataframe <- calculate_CIs(X = X, 
                              proportions = props_mat, 
                              CSSpatialNet_output = csspatialnet_out)
```
